nodes.title: SG-2.1 Author the room shell and furniture grids
nodes.body:
Context: game/frontend/src/art/sources.ts holds only a hand cursor grid, and src/lib/gridToRgba.ts, spriteSheet.ts and generateAssets.ts already turn grids into PNGs. The room art is still SVG. Desired behavior: source grids exist for wall, wainscot, floor, window with night sky, desk, computer, lamp, plant, poster, bookshelf with books and globe, bed, door and rug, each at a declared size, drawn with outlines and ramp shading from the shared 48-colour palette in src/lib/palette.ts. Expected result: unit tests assert each grid's size and that it uses only palette colours. Why: this is the art base for SG-2.2 and SG-2.3. Switching content and manifest to PNGs and deleting SVGs is out of scope.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given the room source registry, when it is loaded, then it contains grids for wall, wainscot, floor, window, desk, computer, lamp, plant, poster, bookshelf, bed, door and rug
- Given each source grid, when its width and height are measured, then they equal the size declared for that id
- Given each source grid, when it is rendered with gridToRgba against PALETTE, then every pixel colour is a palette colour and each grid uses at least 3 distinct palette indices


## Scope
- In scope: Pure drawing helpers
- In scope: Room shell and furniture source grids with declared sizes
- In scope: Unit tests for size and palette use
- Out of scope: Boy sheet and portrait (SG-2.2)
- Out of scope: Switching content and manifest to PNGs and deleting SVGs (SG-2.3)
- Out of scope: BootScene animation loading
- Out of scope: Inventory item icons
- Preserve: Existing ART_SOURCES cursor entry
- Preserve: generateArt CLI and manifest output
- Preserve: Existing SVG assets and manifest entries


## Technical constraints
- All art is raster pixel art generated in the repo from source data by a deterministic script; no downloaded art or CDN
- One native scene resolution of 480x270, whole-number scaling, nearest-neighbour
- One shared palette of at most 48 colours defined once in src/lib/palette.ts
- Tests are unit tests with all dependencies mocked
- Phaser stays on 3.90.x; React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind, Radix and Zustand stay


## Definition of done
- All 13 grids exist at declared sizes
- Size and palette tests pass


## Non-functional requirements
- Drawing code is deterministic and pure, so output is stable between runs


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · Pure grid drawing helpers and a declared-size registry exist
nodes.body:
Context: sources.ts builds grids from character maps only. Desired behavior: pure helper functions create a grid, fill and outline rectangles, apply ramp shading and dither, and map ramp name and step to a PALETTE index. A registry declares width and height for every room art id. Expected result: later grids are built from these helpers against declared sizes. Why: one shared toolkit keeps outlines and shading consistent and testable.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given createGrid(w,h,idx), when called, then it returns an h-row by w-column grid of idx
- Given rampIndex('wood',2), when called, then it returns the PALETTE index of PALETTE_RAMPS.wood[2]
- Given ROOM_ART_SIZES, when read, then it has an entry with positive integer width and height for each of the 13 room ids


## Scope
- In scope: src/art/draw.ts helpers
- In scope: src/art/roomSizes.ts registry
- Out of scope: Any concrete room grid
- Out of scope: Manifest changes
- Preserve: src/lib/palette.ts values
- Preserve: src/lib/gridToRgba.ts behaviour


## Technical constraints
- Shared palette is defined once in src/lib/palette.ts and only referenced
- Pure functions, no I/O or randomness


## Dependencies
- INT


## Definition of done
- Helpers and registry exported and typed


## Clarifying questions
- None

Context: the room shell is one flat SVG. Desired behavior: grids for striped wallpaper (480x150), wood wainscot with trim (480x40), plank floor (480x80) and a window (64x56) with frame, crescent moon and night sky, drawn with outlines and ramp shading from indigo, plum, moon, wood and brass ramps. - Given the wall source, when measured, then it is 480x150 and has alternating wallpaper stripes using two plum or indigo ramp indices

- Given the window source, when measured, then it is 64x56 and contains both moon-ramp and brass-ramp indices

- Out of scope: Furniture
- Out of scope: Manifest or content references
- Preserve: ART_SOURCES

- Only PALETTE indices
- Native 480x270 resolution
- Deterministic, no random

nodes.body:

- 480x270 native resolution: wall+wainscot+floor heights sum to 270

nodes.description: Add pure helpers over number[][] grids that index PALETTE, plus the registry of declared sizes: wall 480x150, wainscot 480x40, floor 480x80, window 64x56, desk 80x32, computer 30x34, lamp 16x30, plant 20x32, poster 28x36, bookshelf 48x96, bed 104x40, door 40x80, rug 80x24. The first three together fill 480x270.
acceptance_criteria: draw.ts exports createGrid, fillRect, outlineRect, shadeRect, dither and rampIndex
roomSizes.ts exports ROOM_ART_SIZES with the 13 declared sizes
technical_constraints: Shared palette of at most 48 colours stays defined once in src/lib/palette.ts
480x270 native resolution: wall+wainscot+floor heights sum to 270

steps.action: Create the file. Import PALETTE_RAMPS from '../lib/palette'. Export rampIndex(ramp: keyof typeof PALETTE_RAMPS, step: number): number returning Object.keys(PALETTE_RAMPS).indexOf(ramp) * 6 + step, and throw an Error when step is not an integer 0-5.
steps.code: export function rampIndex(ramp: keyof typeof PALETTE_RAMPS, step: number): number { if (!Number.isInteger(step) || step < 0 || step > 5) throw new Error(`bad ramp step ${step}`); return Object.keys(PALETTE_RAMPS).indexOf(ramp) * 6 + step; }

steps.action: Export Grid = number[][]. createGrid(w,h,idx) returns Array.from({length:h},()=>Array(w).fill(idx)). fillRect(g,x,y,w,h,idx) sets cells inside the grid bounds, clipping outside ones. outlineRect(g,x,y,w,h,idx) sets only the 1px border of that rectangle via fillRect calls.
steps.expected: createGrid(4,3,1) has 3 rows of 4 ones; fillRect clips without throwing

steps.action: shadeRect(g,x,y,w,h,ramp,lightStep,darkStep) fills row bands from rampIndex(ramp,lightStep) at the top to rampIndex(ramp,darkStep) at the bottom, one band per row, choosing step by Math.round of linear interpolation. dither(g,x,y,w,h,a,b) fills cells with a when (cx+cy)%2===0 else b.
steps.expected: shadeRect on a 1x4 area with steps 4 to 1 yields indices descending in ramp order; dither alternates a and b

steps.action: Export ROOM_ART_SIZES: Record<string,{width:number;height:number}> with keys wall, wainscot, floor, window, desk, computer, lamp, plant, poster, bookshelf, bed, door, rug and the sizes stated in the description, as const-style literal values.
steps.code: export const ROOM_ART_SIZES = { wall:{width:480,height:150}, wainscot:{width:480,height:40}, floor:{width:480,height:80}, window:{width:64,height:56}, desk:{width:80,height:32}, computer:{width:30,height:34}, lamp:{width:16,height:30}, plant:{width:20,height:32}, poster:{width:28,height:36}, bookshelf:{width:48,height:96}, bed:{width:104,height:40}, door:{width:40,height:80}, rug:{width:80,height:24} } as const;
steps.expected: Registry has 13 keys; wall, wainscot and floor heights sum to 270

nodes.description: Build four ArtSource entries using the draw helpers and ROOM_ART_SIZES.
acceptance_criteria: BACKGROUND_SOURCES has ids room/wall, room/wainscot, room/floor and room/window
Each has one frame at its ROOM_ART_SIZES size
technical_constraints: Shared palette of at most 48 colours, referenced via rampIndex

steps.action: Import ArtSource from './sources', helpers from './draw', ROOM_ART_SIZES. wallGrid(): createGrid at wall size filled with rampIndex('plum',2); for every x where Math.floor(x/12)%2===0 fillRect a full-height column of rampIndex('plum',3); shade the top 8 rows with indigo step 1 via dither with plum 2; outline nothing. wainscotGrid(): shadeRect full area wood step 3 to 2, fillRect a 3-row top trim at y 0 with brass step 3, a 1-row shadow at y 3 with wood 0, and panel outlines every 60px (outlineRect y 8, h 28, w 52) using wood step 1 plus a wood step 4 highlight row inside the top edge.
steps.expected: Both functions return grids of 150 and 40 rows by 480 columns

steps.action: floorGrid(): createGrid 480x80 with wood step 3; every 16 rows a fillRect seam row of wood 1; vertical plank joints at x multiples of 48 offset by (row band index*16)%48 using wood 1; dither wood 3/4 on every fourth plank for grain. windowGrid(): createGrid 64x56 with indigo 1 sky, dither indigo 2/indigo 1 in the lower half as stars-free haze, fillRect a 3x3 star cells using moon 5 at (10,8),(40,14),(24,30); draw crescent by filling a 14x14 area at (36,6) with moon 5 then overpainting an offset 12x12 area at (40,4) with indigo 1; frame via outlineRect whole area with brass 1, a second inner outlineRect with brass 4, and a centre cross fillRect of width 2 using brass 3; add curtain strips of plum 3 at x 0-5 and x 58-63 with plum 1 shade columns.
steps.expected: floorGrid is 80x480 and windowGrid is 56x64 containing moon and brass indices

steps.action: Export BACKGROUND_SOURCES: ArtSource[] with four entries {id:'room/wall',path:'worlds/the-boys-room/room/wall.png',frames:[wallGrid()]} and the same for wainscot, floor, window.

steps.action: Import helpers, ROOM_ART_SIZES, ArtSource. Each function starts from createGrid(w,h,0) at its declared size, with index 0 as the empty background. deskGrid: shadeRect top slab rows 0-5 wood 5 to 4, front body wood 3 to 2, legs fillRect wood 1 at both ends, outlineRect with indigo 0. computerGrid: monitor body parchment 2 with outlineRect indigo 0, screen fillRect moon 3 with a moon 5 highlight row, base brass 1. lampGrid: shade fillRect lamp 4 on top 10 rows with lamp 5 highlight column, stem brass 2, base wood 2, outlined indigo 0. plantGrid: pot wood 3 outlined, leaves fillRect using hoodie-free colours: use moon 2 and moon 3 blocks as foliage with dither between them.
steps.expected: Four grids returned at 32x80, 34x30, 30x16 and 32x20 (rows x cols)

steps.action: posterGrid: parchment 4 paper with outlineRect wood 1, a plum 3 figure block and brass 4 title bar. bookshelfGrid 48x96: shadeRect body wood 3 to 2, outlineRect indigo 0, shelf boards at rows 30, 60 and 90 fillRect wood 5 top highlight and wood 1 underside, books as 3-wide vertical rects alternating plum 3, hoodie 3 and lamp 3 with heights 12-16 on the top two shelves, and a globe on the bottom shelf: 12x12 fillRect moon 3 circle approximated by cutting corners, brass 3 stand.
steps.expected: posterGrid is 36x28 and bookshelfGrid is 96x48 containing plum, hoodie, lamp, moon and wood indices

steps.action: bedGrid 104x40: wood 3 frame outlined indigo 0, mattress parchment 4, blanket from row 14 with alternating 6px diamond-like blocks of hoodie 3 and hoodie 2 (checker via dither) with lamp 4 trim row, pillow parchment 5. doorGrid 40x80: wood 3 panel shaded, two inset panel outlines wood 1, brass 4 knob 3x3, outline indigo 0, and bottom 2 rows fillRect lamp 5 for light under the door. rugGrid 80x24: plum 3 field, brass 3 border via outlineRect twice, dither plum 4/plum 3 centre. Export FURNITURE_SOURCES with ids room/desk, room/computer, room/lamp, room/plant, room/poster, room/bookshelf, room/bed, room/door, room/rug and paths worlds/the-boys-room/room/<name>.png, one frame each.
steps.expected: FURNITURE_SOURCES has 9 entries at declared sizes

steps.action: Import BACKGROUND_SOURCES and FURNITURE_SOURCES and export ROOM_SOURCES: ArtSource[] = [...BACKGROUND_SOURCES, ...FURNITURE_SOURCES].
